chains.title: Local-first key-line triage for multi-service incidents

scene.statement: A production alert during an on-call shift creates a need to find the decisive log line across services
scene.rationale: The decision is triggered by an observable triage gap, not by a general interest in developer tooling
assumptions: The synthetic alert and handover scenes represent the pilot's intended use boundary
scene.trigger: A paging alert or a user-reported error while the developer is on call
scene.environment: A terminal with access to multi-service logs
scene.task_context: Locate the decisive log line before deciding whether to escalate or roll back

user.statement: On-call backend developers whose multi-service logs drown the decisive line
user.rationale: Only developers with an unresolved triage scene have the observed problem; satisfied structured-logging teams are a control
assumptions: The developer is also the pilot adoption and escalation decision-maker
user.state: Debugging an incident across several services' logs
user.decision_role: Developer deciding whether to escalate and whether to adopt the tool

pain.statement: Manual grep chains and per-service dashboards cannot isolate the decisive line quickly enough
pain.rationale: The selected users' current substitutes fail in the identified scene and produce a slow or wrong escalation decision
assumptions: The observed triage delay matters enough to justify a bounded pilot
pain.current_substitute: Grep chains, per-service dashboards, or hosted APM ingest
pain.friction_cost: Noise lines outnumber decisive events, context switching between services, or shipping raw logs off-site
pain.consequence: Slow escalation decisions and long time-to-restore

need.statement: Isolate the decisive events promptly without shipping raw logs to a third party
need.rationale: The pain implies a solution-neutral triage outcome; it does not by itself prove that a CLI tool is the right answer
assumptions: Prompt local triage is valuable even when no escalation follows
need.desired_outcome: Decide escalate-or-roll-back without reading the full log stream
constraints: No raw log upload to third-party services
No per-service manual greps during an incident
need.measure: Time to a triage decision and unnecessary escalations avoided in a bounded team pilot

feature.statement: A local-first key-line extraction CLI with an explicit redaction switch
feature.rationale: On-demand extraction addresses the triage need while local-only processing and default redaction answer the observed privacy rejection
assumptions: Redaction guarantees remain understandable and effective outside the prototype setting
feature.capability: Extract and rank decisive lines from local logs only during an explicit triage command, with redaction on by default and no network calls
alternatives_considered: Ship logs to a hosted APM

product.rationale: The triage command and its redaction guarantees form the smallest coherent pilot that can test the need, solution acceptance and retained behavior together
assumptions: A two-week pilot is sufficient to reject an unusable or unwanted concept, but not to estimate market demand
product.form: A CLI tool with a rules file, run inside the developer's terminal
product.scope: Two-week pilot for key-line triage on one team's services
non_goals: Replacement for a full APM stack
acceptance_criteria: Pilot developers complete the triage task
Redaction is used without unresolved objections
Predeclared retained-use threshold is met during the pilot

business.statement: Run a bounded paid team pilot before making any subscription, launch, or market-expansion decision
business.rationale: The tool creates a testable value loop, while a bounded paid pilot is the smallest business experiment that can test payment and retained behavior without pretending to prove a sustainable company
assumptions: A real pilot can recruit eligible teams without changing their redaction or usage behavior
Pilot support and delivery costs can be measured before any scale decision
business.market_definition: On-call backend developers in multi-service teams within an illustrative developer-tooling sample
included_markets: Incident log triage through a local-first CLI
business.target_segment: Developers who cannot isolate decisive lines with their current setup and are eligible for a supervised two-week pilot

segments.criteria: On-call developers with multi-service log noise and no satisfactory triage alternative
segments.payer: The team lead who reserves the pilot seat

business.payer: The team lead who reserves and pays a refundable pilot seat deposit
business.positioning: A local-first alternative to adding grep aliases or shipping logs to a hosted APM; not an observability-suite replacement
business.revenue_model: Refundable pilot seat deposit only; no subscription or long-term revenue is assumed
business.pricing_hypothesis: Payment behavior is observed only for the synthetic pilot deposit; final pricing and elasticity remain unknown
channels: Synthetic direct pilot recruitment in developer communities
competitive_alternatives: No change to the current setup

market_estimates.population_definition: Not estimated from the synthetic convenience sample
market_estimates.method: Requires an external sampling frame and paid-demand evidence before estimation

unit_economics_inputs.metric: Rules maintenance and pilot support cost

success_metrics.definition: Developers still actively using the triage command at the end of the pilot
success_metrics.guardrail: Redaction rejection, unresolved support burden, or drop-off crosses the predeclared threshold

gate.resource_commitment: Synthetic fixture only; no real budget or launch resource is committed
gate.revisit_trigger: Redaction rejection, task failure, retained-use, or cost threshold fails

alternative_explanations: Structured logging with alert routing may already surface decisive events for teams without noise problems
Redaction and local-only concerns may outweigh the value of faster triage even with the proposed guarantees

human_review.notes: Illustrates the review contract; no real semantic approval occurred
human_review.risk_acceptance: No real product or launch approval is implied

prioritization.method: Synthetic gate choice: test redaction, acceptance and retained use before any scale decision

factors.consequence: redaction rejection would invalidate the pilot

prioritization.decided_at: Synthetic fixture; no real decision date
prioritization.rationale: The pilot is prioritized as the smallest test that can reverse the concept; no market-size ranking is claimed

change_log.impact: Added redaction guarantees and bounded product scope
change_log.decision: Keep redaction and retention as predeclared pilot gates
change_log.decided_at: Synthetic fixture; no real decision date

gaps: Redaction guarantees are not tested in real teams
The feature-to-product rationale still requires a real bounded pilot; evidence completeness does not prove product success
chains.next_test: Run a real two-week team pilot with predeclared redaction-rejection, task-success and retained-use thresholds
